newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Chubby beauty queen is ad-man's nightmare.
newsitem.headline: Chubby beauty queen is ad-man's nightmare.

text.p: Kellogg Co. said on Monday it will discontinue Special K breakfast cereal boxes featuring Venezuela's reigning Miss Universe Alicia Machado, dubbed "the eating machine" by the pageant's organisers.

Following a series of heated letters in the local press by disillusioned Special K buyers complaining about Machado's weight gain, a Kellogg spokeswoman told Reuters on Monday: "We've decided to discontinue the campaign."
In Venezuela, where beauty queen titles launch political careers, Kellogg's Special K cereal boxes featured the 19-year old brunette sitting on an inflatable globe above the slogan "nothing to hide."
Buyers who stocked up on the cereal in the hope of keeping their figures trim now want their money back.

Machado, whose term as Miss Universe ends in May, acknowledged in September she had gained about 11 pounds (5 kg). There were rumours the Miss Universe organisation had threatened to strip her of her crown unless she went on a crash diet.

"A lot of people have wanted to take the title away from her, but I say, let her keep it," Miss Universe organisation president Donald Trump said in a recent television interview. "She'd be destroyed if they take it away."
But he admitted: "She's eating a lot. You could say she's an eating machine."
